blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Historical 2026-07-30 review of the sole tracked Monad lvUSD deployment 0xfd44b35139ae53fff7d8f2a9869c503d987f00d1 identified blackList(address), updateBlackList(address,bool) gated by only operator, and owner-controlled setOperator(address), establishing a direct token-level holder-freeze surface. At Monad block 109550480 on 2026-10-01, owner() and issuer() still resolved to the VMMV engine 0x135951057cfccca7e8ef87ee41318d670f723f68, which was owned by the 3-of-5 Safe 0xf9bd99a8e5be72adf687b304ed0e0234e0ebccba; operator() now returned 0x9f61b30f5607f71ad9e5288c8d9b648da9076eb4, rather than the zero operator observed in July. A current blacklister is therefore appointed under the historically verified operator gate. This read does not enumerate all currently blacklisted holders or establish when the operator changed. The July token-code review found no separate pause selector. Upstream Circle USDC collateral freezes remain a separate inherited reserve exposure, not the lvUSD token control path.

oracleRisk.summary: LeverUp describes lvUSD as a USDC-backed liquidity-layer token stabilized through protocol-internal TWAP anchoring, LV auctions, and redemption quotas rather than an external liquidation oracle.

branchApplicability.rationale: LeverUp documents lvUSD as a liquidity-layer asset whose peg is managed by protocol-internal TWAP anchoring, LV auctions, and redemption quotas. Those internal price and redemption controls are a top-level authority; the product does not expose borrower-owned collateral positions or per-market liquidation branches to inventory.
